sec: Hypokalemia treatment and the opening of hyperkalemia

items.q: What does the acute-attack line prescribe for potassium chloride infusion, and how much potassium does one ampoule contain?
opts: 2 ampoules in 300 mL normal saline over 2 hours, 10 mEq per ampoule
1 ampoule in 500 mL normal saline over 4 hours, 20 mEq per ampoule
2 ampoules in 100 mL dextrose over 1 hour, 5 mEq per ampoule
4 ampoules in 300 mL normal saline over 2 hours, 10 mEq per ampoule
items.exp: The acute attack is treated with KCl, 2 ampoules in 300 mL N.S over 2 hours, with 1 ampoule equal to 10 mEq and 1 mL of KCl equal to 2 mEq. (Book p973)

items.q: State the peripheral-line rate ceiling and the maximum permissible daily dose given on this page.
items.exp: The two safety lines are a maximum rate of 20 mEq/hr through a peripheral line and a maximum permissible dose of 160 mEq per day. (Book p973)

items.q: Fill up: The 160 mEq daily ceiling is annotated as raising the serum potassium by ______ mEq/L, and the maintenance requirement given for potassium is ______ mEq/day.
items.exp: The bracket after 160 mEq/day reads an increase in K+ of 2 mEq/L, and the maintenance section opens with a required dose of 75 mEq/day. (Book p973)

items.q: A ward prescription reads potassium chloride 4 ampoules in 300 mL saline to run over 2 hours peripherally. Which single figure on this page makes that order unsafe?
opts: The maximum rate of 20 mEq/hr through a peripheral line
The strength of 2 mEq in each millilitre of KCl
The total daily limit of 75 mEq
items.exp: Four ampoules give 40 mEq, and running that in 2 hours means 20 mEq/hr only if the whole volume is given over 2 hours, whereas the printed acute order is 2 ampoules; 40 mEq in under 2 hours would exceed the stated peripheral ceiling of 20 mEq/hr. (Book p973)

items.q: How much potassium and bicarbonate does potassium citrate syrup deliver per 5 mL, and what daily volume does the page estimate?
opts: 10 mEq of potassium only, about 35 mL/day
items.exp: Maintenance option 1 is K+ citrate syrup, 5 mL providing 10 mEq each of K+ and HCO3-, at roughly 35 mL per day. (Book p973)

items.q: Match each indication with the bicarbonate dose printed for it — 1) Distal RTA 2) Proximal RTA 3) Extra bicarbonate as Shohl's solution … A) 1 mL provides 1 mEq of HCO3- B) 2 to 4 mEq/kg/day C) 10 to 15 mEq/kg/day
items.exp: The HCO3- requirement block gives 2-4 mEq/kg/day for distal RTA and 10-15 mEq/kg/day for proximal RTA, with Shohl's solution, a sodium citrate and citric acid mixture, supplying 1 mEq per mL. (Book p973)

items.q: Assess the two oral options: I A 750 mg KCl tablet supplies 10 mEq of potassium and needs multiple dosing. II The tablet also corrects any accompanying acidosis.
items.exp: The tablet block lists 750 mg equal to 10 mEq K+, multiple dosing required and, explicitly, acidosis not corrected, which is why the citrate syrup is preferred when bicarbonate is also needed. (Book p973)

items.q: A patient with diarrhoea-induced hypokalemia and a hyperchloraemic acidosis needs oral replacement. Which choice on this page serves both problems?
items.exp: The citrate syrup supplies 10 mEq each of potassium and bicarbonate per 5 mL, whereas the chloride tablet is annotated as not correcting acidosis. (Book p973)

items.q: Hyperkalemia is introduced on this page with which two-word characterisation?
items.exp: The hyperkalemia heading carries the single line acute emergency before the causes tree. (Book p973)

items.q: Match each column of the hyperkalemia causes tree with the entries printed under it — 1) Renal 2) Spurious 3) Cellular shift … A) Nothing is written beneath this heading on the page B) Renal failure, the most common, and RTA type 4 from aldosterone insufficiency C) Thrombocytosis, fragile cells in chronic lymphocytic leukemia, trauma during blood collection and repeated clenching of the fist
items.exp: The renal column lists renal failure as the most common cause and RTA-IV, the spurious column has four entries, and the cellular-shift column is left blank in the printed scheme. (Book p973)

items.q: All of the following are placed under the spurious column EXCEPT:
opts: Fragile cells in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
items.exp: ATN belongs to the renal column through renal failure, while the spurious list covers thrombocytosis, fragile CLL cells, collection trauma and repeated fist clenching, all in-vitro potassium releases. (Book p973)

items.q: A laboratory report shows potassium 6.9 mEq/L in an asymptomatic patient whose platelet count is 950 x 10^9/L and whose sample was drawn through a difficult, haemolysing venepuncture. Which column of this page's tree explains the result?
opts: Spurious, through thrombocytosis and collection trauma
Renal, through undisclosed acute kidney injury
Cellular shift, through a beta-blocker effect
None, since potassium cannot rise outside the body
items.exp: Two of the four spurious entries, thrombocytosis and trauma during blood collection, are present, so the elevation is a laboratory artefact rather than a patient problem. (Book p973)

items.q: Assess the renal column: I Renal failure is described as the most common renal cause. II RTA type 4 is annotated with aldosterone insufficiency.
items.exp: The two renal entries are 1 renal failure with the abbreviation m/c and 2 RTA-IV with aldosterone insufficiency in brackets, the subject of the next page. (Book p973)
